doc.title: Ken Peplowski interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 10, 1997 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Peps, humorous titles and the Caligula musical joke
summary: Banter about his nickname, joke credits, Caligula, and his love of humorists.

story.theme_name: How I got my name: nicknames and band monikers
story.community_name: How I got my name: nicknames and band names

blocks.x: Well I wanted to ask you about “Steppin’ with Peps.” Most people call you “Peps?”
A lot of people do. Pep, Peps, yeah.
You have one of your own tunes on here, “Huggles,” which you, I think you have a sense of humor. You announce one tune here as “one by Benny Aranoff” is that —
— with his usual sly wit and then your own tune is “Me and My Half Wit.”
Actually I wanted to ask you how this project, you were born at an early age, really, working on your next project — Caligula, the musical.

I always thought that that was such a strange idea. You know, an all-singing, all-dancing version of Caligula. Two things you would never expect to go together you know. And I’ve actually had people ask me, seriously, about that. Like are you really working on that?
You could do a double bill with “Annie.”
Yes. Annie the Tragedy. The Lost Years. Annie on 42nd Street. No but hey look, you have to have a sense of humor to do this you know. But what was your question anyway?
I don’t know if there was a question. I just got a kick out of reading that.
I wanted to bring it up.

I actually think about writing some things because I like to do that. And the last record I did I wrote my own liner notes too and I think you would get a kick out of those. And I also am a big fan of the old New Yorker humorists, Robert Benchley and S.J. Perelman. I love to read those kind of people. And that’s kind of gone now. You don’t see that kind of writing anymore.
